breaking_changes: GET /api/v1/system-stats now reports the scalar gpu_percent and vram_gb fields for the primary GPU by total memory instead of the GPU with the highest utilization — on multi-GPU systems the numbers meaningfully change and existing dashboards or alerting based on those fields will see different values.

Models gated behind a guest-tier backend are now hidden from GET /v1/models?show_all=true and return model_not_supported on pull until the guest backend is installed — existing setups that relied on the model being visible without the backend will see them disappear.

evidence.blockers: Four P0 items must clear before shipping: the backend lifecycle refactoring must handle multiple backends correctly without process leaks, guest-backend model gating must work end-to-end so users can pull models after installing required backends, multi-GPU primary GPU selection must return correct metrics for monitoring, and the FLM v1.0.7 rollback must fix the systemd launch failure on NPU hardware.
evidence.breaking_changes: Two breaking changes ship in this release: (1) GET /api/v1/system-stats now reports gpu_percent and vram_gb for the primary GPU by total memory instead of the highest-utilization GPU — on multi-GPU systems these values change meaningfully and existing dashboards will see different numbers; (2) models gated behind guest-tier backends are now hidden from GET /v1/models?show_all=true and return model_not_supported on pull until the guest backend is installed — existing setups that relied on the model being visible without the backend will see them disappear.
evidence.coverage: All 21 commits in the v2026.42.1 to b48d190a9b00a417fda9cbf206fcec5691e5578b range were reviewed. Each commit received at least one reviewer assessment; no PRs in the range lack a digest entry.
evidence.manual_testing: Human verification required on: (1) multi-GPU hardware with mixed NVIDIA and AMD GPUs to validate the primary GPU selection change, (2) Strix Halo NPU systems to verify guest-backend model gating, (3) Windows machines with AMD discrete GPUs for the new DXCore/PDH telemetry path, (4) real image files for multi-reference editing and soft-pixel-cap behavior, and (5) an NPU device under systemd to confirm the FLM rollback.
evidence.security: No security concerns observed. The Windows AMD telemetry path uses safe DLL loading with LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_SYSTEM32. The guest-backend gating is a safety improvement that prevents accidental installation of externally-maintained backends. No supply-chain, credential, or code-execution changes detected across the release.
